body.name: Fixed-class bounded-outcome minimax games
body.construction:
For an integer \(K_0\ge2\), write \(\mathcal A_{K_0}=\{1,\ldots,K_0\}\).  Fix \(n\ge1\), real numbers \(L<U\), a contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^{K_0}\), and a nonempty class \(\mathfrak D\) of assignment laws on \(\mathcal A_{K_0}^n\), every member of which is selected independently of the potential-outcome schedule.  For \(\mathcal I=[L,U]\) or \(\mathcal I=\{0,1\}\), define
\[
 R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,\mathcal I}(c)
 =\inf_{\mathcal D_n\in\mathfrak D}\ \inf_{\delta}
   \sup_{w\in\mathcal I^{n\times K_0}}
   \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,\delta}\!\left[
   \left\{\delta\bigl((A_i,w_{i,A_i})_{i=1}^n\bigr)
   -\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a=1}^{K_0}c_aw_{i,a}
   \right\}^2\right],
\]
where the second infimum is over all possibly randomized Markov kernels from the labeled observed data to \(\mathbb R\), and the expectation includes both assignment and estimator randomization.  Write these two risks as \(R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,[L,U]}(c)\) and \(R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,\{0,1\}}(c)\).  When the first infimum ranges over all outcome-independent assignment laws, abbreviate them by \(R_{n,[L,U]}(c)\) and \(R_{n,\{0,1\}}(c)\), respectively.  Thus \(R_{n,\{0,1\}}(c)=R_n(c)\) in the binary game of \(\mathrm{def:risk\text{-}game}\).
